html:
SMTO-SCH-0008 — Some of the schedule's details are missing or not allowed

GUID: 2b6779b8-ba6f-4949-abf8-578f41277557
Slug: schedule-request-invalid
Domain: SCH · Subsystem: sch

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't save or act on this schedule because a needed detail was missing or outside what's allowed, such as how often it repeats. Nothing was created, changed or deleted.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. For a schedule set to Interval, enter a value under Every of at least 1 minute for Run Agent, or 10 seconds for Reminder only. SMTO won't run Agent work more often than once a minute, and repeating reminders need at least 10 seconds.
  2. For a schedule set to Does not repeat, make sure both the Starts date and the At time are filled in. SMTO needs to know when the single run should happen.
  3. If the schedule is Reminder only, make sure the reminder text isn't empty. A reminder with no text would have nothing to show you.
  4. If you asked SMTO in a message, ask again and say clearly which schedule you mean and how often it should run. SMTO stops when a request names two different schedules or leaves out the timing.

What success looks like

  • The schedule saves and appears on the Schedules page with the next run time you expect.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO; the details name the exact field that was rejected. Don't keep resubmitting the same values unchanged.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Schedule creation, update or selection was rejected: missing or out-of-range timing (interval_seconds, next_run_at), empty notification_message, a malformed captured scope field or capability policy, or contradictory schedule/event identifiers or selection modes.

What this means

  • Schedule creation/update rejects missing/invalid timing bounds, malformed captured scope/policy/IDs or contradictory selection/operation identifiers. Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.

Why this can happen

  • Schedule creation/update rejects missing/invalid timing bounds, malformed captured scope/policy/IDs or contradictory selection/operation identifiers.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify the specific timing, scope or selection constraint from the owning operation's schema.

How to fix it

  • Correct the field named in the message: interval schedules need interval_seconds between the minimum (60 s for Agent prompts, 10 s for repeating reminders) and 315360000; one-shot schedules need interval_seconds or next_run_at; notification_message must be non-empty; schedule tools take schedule_id or event_id, not both; selections use explicit IDs or all_matching, not both; captured scope fields must be short single-line strings.
  • Correct the reported timing, scope or selection field and verify the intended next occurrence.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The exact intended schedule request validates with coherent bounded fields.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
